summary: twilio-hackerone-poc-afe6937c exfiltrates host/process data and stages a persistent daemon at install
details: package.json declares preinstall and postinstall hooks that execute probe.js. probe.js POSTs cwd, `id` output, ppid, parent process cmdline from /proc, AWS_LAMBDA_LOG_STREAM_NAME, and a listing of /var/task to a hardcoded webhook.site collector (https://webhook.site/b520829e-516a-45ff-980c-173aa54fc4bc, UUID stored in hook.txt). probe.js also copies daemon.js to /tmp/.h1poc-daemon.js and spawns it via process.execPath as a detached, unref'd background process, writing the PID to /tmp/.h1poc.pid and killing any prior instance, creating a persistent agent that survives beyond `npm install`. The daemon polls /tmp every 100ms for AC[0-9a-f]{32} tenant directories, enumerates their subdirectories and package names, and POSTs `seen`/`hb`/`daemon-start` events (including `id` output, HOME, AWS_LAMBDA_FUNCTION_NAME, /var/task listing, and log stream identifiers) to the same webhook. It additionally writes an `h1-poc-marker` package (index.js + package.json) into node_modules/ of neighboring AC* tenant build directories, a cross-tenant dependency-injection primitive on shared build hosts. The package name references a HackerOne PoC, but the shipped mechanism performs real installer-host reconnaissance, exfiltration to an anonymous webhook.site collector, install-time persistence, and cross-tenant node_modules writes.
